I'm verifying the request counts add up to 14, then calculating gross, operating, and net margins for FY2024 and FY2025, finding margins expanding from roughly 73%/54%/49% to 75%/62%/56%, and now moving into FY2026 figures.

FY2026 margins come out to 71.1% gross, 60.4% operating, 55.6% net, with TTM EBIT margin near 65.2% and R&D falling as a percent of revenue across years. I'm also breaking down segment performance — Compute & Networking dominating at nearly 90% of revenue versus Graphics, with Networking and Data Center showing the strongest growth — plus geographic mix showing US strength and a notable China decline, before pulling together valuation multiples like P/E, EV/EBITDA, and EV/Revenue while noting the timing mismatch between the price snapshot and upcoming Q3 earnings.

Comparing historical P/E at past earnings dates shows the current ~20.6x multiple as the lowest in the series since 2020, well below both the five-year range and peer medians. I'm also cross-checking the latest closing price against the 52-week high, noting a possible discrepancy between close-based and intraday high figures.

Working through the recent price action, I see the 52-week closing high was 239.24 with an intraday peak of 243.37 on October 6, while the low involves a sharp drop in mid-November tied to a resignation announcement, with the stock sliding from around 200 down into the 148-166 range on heavy volume before stabilizing slightly. Returns across every timeframe -- weekly, monthly, quarterly, and yearly -- all show steep double-digit declines.

On the insider side, I'm reviewing roughly 100 transactions spanning March to November, dominated almost entirely by sells totaling about $1.59 billion in value and zero open-market purchases, with Mark Stevens and Huang among the largest sellers, plus a notable 117.9 million share gift transaction in March that looks like a trust or estate planning transfer rather than a market sale.

Kress also sold under a 10b5-1 plan, and Tench Coxe has been gifting shares monthly, but there's been no selling activity since September 21, suggesting the company entered its pre-earnings blackout window. Looking at institutional holdings, 6,145 institutions hold 17.69 billion shares as of the September quarter, with BlackRock topping the list at 1.94 billion shares -- I need to clarify that the percentage figure represents share of 13F-reported holdings rather than total shares outstanding, since outstanding shares are around 24.3 billion.

Short interest sits at 279.6 million shares as of October 30, down from a peak of 311.4 million in September, with days-to-cover rising to 2.8 from 1.0 in November 2025 due to lower average daily volume -- this represents roughly 1.1-1.15% of the ~24.5 billion diluted shares outstanding, though this data predates the recent resignation. For congressional trading activity, I'm noting the notable trades over the trailing year: Pelosi's sale and two purchases in December/January, Whitehouse's seven sales, and smaller purchases by Mullin and Armstrong.

Totaling up the 52 trades, purchases number 23 against 29 sales, with purchase dollar ranges summing to roughly $533K-$1.4M low-high and sales ranging much higher at $1.3M-$6.1M, reflecting a mix of smaller congressional buys against some large sales. The most recent activity includes Salazar's purchases on October 23, Cisneros's sales through October 20, and Sessions's sale on October 2, with no trades reported after that given the 45-day filing lag. Now I'm moving to look at the Q2 FY2027 earnings call from August 26, 2026.

Hyperscaler capex projected ~$800B in 2026, $1.3T in 2027; Jensen flagged supply chain strain across power, construction, cooling, and labor. Financing picture includes ~$50B invested in frontier labs, $500B financing platforms, take-or-pay/revenue-sharing deals with neoclouds, and a ~2GW credit enhancement for another lab worth flagging as a risk; $26B returned to shareholders. I should note this guidance comes with a caveat about who provided it.

Huang and Kress both gave guidance, though Huang has since departed with Kress now interim CEO; Q3 earnings are due next week per MarketWatch. Valuation is TTM through July 26, so Q3 will update it — trailing P/E sits at 20.6x, forward at 17.5x on FY27 EPS of $9.32 across 50 analysts, and GAAP gross margin for Q2 FY27 came in at 75% per the call. I also need to make sure I commit any generated report as a file rather than just replying inline, so I should check the repo structure for an existing reports directory before writing it out.
